data.body: Phase 1 RCA — confirmed defect. Mechanism: .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml places the OS/Python-invariant Complexity-baseline lock step inside jobs.test, whose 4-cell matrix executes that same commit-level policy once per Ubuntu 3.11/3.12/3.13 and macOS 3.12 cell. Runtime proof from Gerrit Verify logs observed 52s, 54s, 55s, and 45s step durations (206 runner-seconds total); one execution at the slowest observed 52s would preserve the same policy result, so approximately 154 runner-seconds are duplicate work. The near-equal duration across all cells and identical command rule out a single-platform/test-runtime explanation. Defect legitimacy: the explicit session contract requires lower wall-clock and runner use without reducing policy/test coverage, while the lock compares a commit-level artifact to main and has no OS/Python-dependent behavior. Caller-dependency sweep: both lint and test jobs check out the same Gerrit patchset; the reusable workflow and final vote wait for the whole build-and-test workflow, so moving the unchanged fail-closed step to jobs.lint remains blocking. No caller depends on four executions. OSS precedent recorded in the plan: CPython/Django centralize lint policy in one lint job; Rust/Kubernetes use one tidy/verify surface. Expected repair: exactly one unchanged lock invocation in jobs.lint and none in jobs.test; no jobs, runners, dependencies, or coverage removed.
